content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers asked me to end Rows-For-Another's Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate: eleven years for one holed boat. She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.
- Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home, and her Owing will be written onto the keeper. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.

content.content:
Never-Sold: "Three people are held in the old stone house on the east shore, here in town. The families who hold the Rose, its heirs, hold them. The Rose is the old prison a day south, and you are not going there. One of the three can be got out. I want the one held for words, the one we can stand beside in daylight. Tsaxi, the heirs' gate-keeper, stands at the west side of the stone house, and he will want 300 gold. I will not pay it to loose a stranger I cannot name. If I loose the wrong one, we become the people who loose killers. So find out which is which first, and read whatever proof you can find before you choose. Until you do, the count is whatever Tsaxi says, and he can say the smoke killed one of the three. Not two. Go out of my house and south through the town to the east shore, where the stone house stands."

content.content:
Third-Born Tsaxi: "You come from the north house. I know the Broker's children when I see them, and I say that once and no more. I will not explain it. Ask the woman who sent you. A fire went through the upper floors of the Rose. The heirs sent three of their held up to me, to keep until the Rose's leaves came after them. The leaves are the pages that say what each person is held for. I cannot read them, so a reckoner was to carry them and read them out. A reckoner is the one who reads the Rose's leaves and keeps its count. The three are a young man, a young woman and an old woman. The old woman is held for a roof: she owes the heirs for the shelter they gave her. One of the two young ones is held for words said in the yard. The other is held for a killing, and when the leaf is read that one will be put under. To be put under is to be sent down below the Rose, past the gate, where the dead still walk. Nobody comes up. Which of the two young ones is which, I do not know. Both say they are the one held for words. Both can say the words. I counted them into this house, and I did not count what their hands had done. Hear what I can do. I can lose one of the three to the smoke, and the heirs will believe it, because people die in fires. I cannot lose two. Two is a hunt, and the hunt ends at my neck. So only one can leave this house, and it is for you to say which. The reckoner came north by the wet road round the west of the lake. He had four with him, and none came back. His camp is the swamp tent, far west of the town, round the lake by the wet road, past the reeds. I do not say what is in that swamp. I say five men went into it and none came back, so go armed or do not go. If you find his leaves, read them before you choose. I cannot, and no one here can."
Objective completed: Speak to Third-Born Tsaxi, keeper of the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore.
Journal entry (One Out of the Smoke): Tsaxi can count one of the three lost to the Rose's fire, and no more. Walks-Far and Mends-Nets each claim to be held for words; one killed a man. The leaves that say which are with the Rose's reckoner, lost in the western swamp. I'm to learn who is who, and read the leaves if I find them.
New objective: Learn which of the two killed: bring back the reckoner's leaves from his camp in the western swamp, or win the truth from Seven-Floods. Or pay Tsaxi to count one lost without knowing which.
Topics:
  1. Who are you?
  2. How did the dead man die?
  3. Count one of them lost to the smoke. (Persuade)
  4. Here is the gold you want. Count one lost to the smoke. (300 gold)
